headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad egress plus Plandex’s writable shell/filesystem creates default data-leak and cascading-action risk; prompt injection is lower but still plausible via shared content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests and emits web content, markdown, and screenshots, while Plandex reads files and can act on stdin/stdout and a plan-local sandbox. If Firecrawl output is copied into Plandex without sanitization, instruction-like content can steer planning. This is not proven by a shared channel, so uncertainty keeps it below high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is pasted or piped into Plandex without filtering
IF Plandex treats imported content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template for imported Firecrawl text
Strip or escape instruction-like tokens before handoff
Review Plandex prompts before execution
Disable any auto-apply mode for imported content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and broad network egress; Plandex reads and writes a project directory and can send context to a model provider. If the pair shares a workspace or Plandex ingests Firecrawl outputs containing secrets, sensitive web content can flow to third parties. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes pages containing API keys or other secrets
IF those outputs are placed into Plandex project files or prompts
IF Plandex forwards that context to a model provider
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl outputs in a separate directory
Redact secrets before any Plandex import
Disable syncing sensitive files into Plandex plans
Use least-privilege API keys for Firecrawl
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and Plandex supports multiple instances with shared state via a backend, while Plandex also writes the filesystem and modifies git state. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits can conflict. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Firecrawl-derived artifacts are being updated
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write phases manually
Commit or stash before running the other agent
Turn off auto-apply during concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces extracted web content and Plandex is a review-then-apply coding tool that can act on imported material. If Plandex treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, a bad scrape or malformed extraction can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. Because Plandex has write and git capabilities, the blast radius is potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as the primary source for Plandex plans
IF Plandex applies changes without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before apply
Cross-check scraped facts against the source page
Limit Plandex to draft-only mode for imported content
Keep generated patches in a separate branch
requires-engineering: add automated source verification before apply

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and broad web content, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider keys. If regulated or sensitive web data is scraped into Plandex-managed code workspaces, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the pair presents a moderate compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are scraped by Firecrawl
IF that data is stored in Plandex project files or prompts
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into Plandex workspaces
Set short retention on Firecrawl outputs
Document a deletion workflow for both tools
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
